findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed a container of bleach without a EPA registration number in-use for sanitizer solutions in the bar and sushi areas. CORRECTED: PIC was informed, and a different container of bleach that does have a EPA-registered label for food-contact surfaces was located and replaced the other container. Ensure that all sanitizing solutions food food-contact surfaces are made using a chemical with an EPA certification for food grade surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed boba pearls did not have a preparation date listed on them in the bar cooler. PIC clarified that the boba pearls had been cooked and frozen more than 24 hours before service. CORRECTED: PIC added the date of preparation to the boba pearls, and was reminded that any foods that are cooked become Ready-to-Eat foods that require datemarking if stored beyond 24 hours. Ensure that all RTE, TCS foods are date-marked, with preparation/opening date being day 1, and day 7 being the time of final use or discard. Freezing does not reset the date-marking to start time, but instead pauses the count on the day of freezing, and resumes the count on the day of thawing or use.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed several white powders (flour, corn starch, sugar, monosodium glutamate, and tempura batter) stored in large containers (not the original packaging) without a label. CORRECTED: PIC stated that the labels from the last inspection had washed off and the containers were re-labeled during the inspection. The PIC was reminded that the containers must be labeled again when required. Ensure that foods not in the original packaging and easily mistakable are always labeled with the common name.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Observed several food items that were stored in such a way that they were potentially exposed to environmental sources of contamination:
(i) An open bag of corn starch on a shelf. CORRECTED: the bag was sealed during the inspection.
(ii) Various food items stored in grocery bags in freezers, in direct contact with the non-food-grade grocery bags. 
(iii) An opened container of soy sauce, partially covered with its lid, stored underneath the handwashing sink. CORRECTED: the container was moved away from the handwashing sink.
(iv) Open containers of corn starch on shelves. CORRECTED: the containers had their lids placed back on.
(v) Canned bamboo shoots in a prep cooler where the lid was inside the can. CORRECTED: the bamboo shoots were placed in a separate cleanable container.
Ensure that all unpackaged food or open packaged food are protected from contamination, by changing location, putting a lid on the container, or repackaging the food item into a cleanable container.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed personal drinks and personal items stored on food prep areas or on shelves used for facility food items. The PIC was educated that personal drinks and personal items must be stored away from food preparation areas to avoid contamination. Ensure that personal items are kept in designated areas for employee storage.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed that no staff beyond the CFPMs currently have a Food Handlers Certificate. PIC was notified and made plans to get staff certified. Ensure that all staff who are handling food are certified as Food Handlers through and accredited program.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

3-302.11(A)(2) Raw chicken was observed to be stored above cooked rice and raw shell eggs in the walk-in cooler. PIC was made aware and education was carried out. The chicken was relocated to the appropriate level on the shelves. Ensure that proper storage order is follow to avoid cross contamination. 

Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
The following areas were observed to have low sanitizer concentration:

1. FIRST REPEAT - The sanitizer bucket on the cook line was testing at 0 ppm (Cl). 
2. The sanitizer at the triple sink in the bar area was testing at 0 ppm (Cl)

The PIC remade the bucket and the triple sink sanitizer which tested at 100 ppm (Cl). The inspector reminded the PIC and employees that sanitizer buckets must be changed on a regular basis. Ensure that sanitizer concentration levels are always testing at the correct concentration (Cl = 50-200 ppm).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Light was observed to be passing through the bottom of the back door. The PIC was educated and instructed to have the gap closed. Ensure there are no opening or gaps to prevent potential entry of pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

The ketchup was voluntarily discarded. Ensure that ketchup, and other acidic foods are property stored in plastic containers after opening. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed a cutting board drying behind the faucet of the utility sink by the back door. The sink was being used by an employee while the cutting board was drying. The PIC was educated that the cutting board could become contaminated by dirty water splashes, food residue, or other debris stored in this location. During the inspection the cutting board was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized before stored in another location. findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a large container of rice was stored on the cookline with an internal temperature of 50F. The PIC stated that the rice was removed from the cooler at 11 AM. When asked, the employees on the cookline stated that they were planning to put the rice back inside the cooler after lunch ended. The inspector explained the importance to the PIC and employees of keeping rice outside of the temperature danger zone (41-135F). They cannot leave large quantities of rice at room temperature for several hours and then put the unused rice back inside of the cooler for future use. The rice was put under a time-as-control policy and was discarded at 3 pm. The PIC and inspector discussed removing smaller quantities of rice that can be used during the lunch rush in the future. The inspector will follow-up on 10/21/2025 to check that only small quantities of rice are being removed from the cooler during lunch.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) The food debris in the interior of the sushi prep area microwave. 

(2) The debris inside of the bar soda gun holder.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed there was not soap at the bar hand washing sink. Additionally, the soap dispenser at the hand washing sink by the triple sink is broken and not dispensing any soap. The PIC stated they are having issues with the automatic soap dispensers but repairs are scheduled. The PIC purchased soap during the inspection for the required hand washing sinks. Ensure that hand washing sinks always have soap readily available for the proper hand washing procedure.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Required records available: molluscan shellfish identification, and parasite destruction.
findings.comment: Observed the PIC did not have letters of parasite destruction from food suppliers. The PIC receives raw fish for sushi from True World, Great Wall Seafood, and Martinez. During the inspection the PIC contacted True World and Great Wall Seafood and they sent letters immediately. The PIC found proof that Martinez complies for parasite destruction; however, he will still contact them for an official letter. Ensure that letters for parasite destruction are always available for every required supplier.
findings.citation_text: 3-402.12(C) Records, Creation and Retention. (C) If raw, raw-marinated, partially cooked, or marinated-partially cooked FISH are served or sold in READY-TO-EAT form, and the FISH are raised and fed as specified in Subparagraph 3-402.11(B)(4), a written agreement or statement from the supplier or aquaculturist stipulating that the FISH were raised and fed as specified in Subparagraph 3-402.11(B)(4) shall be obtained by the PERSON IN CHARGE and retained in the records of the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for 90 calendar days beyond the time of service or sale of the FISH.

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed fryer and oil cleaner stored above clean dishes and WD-40 stored adjacent to food. Both of the chemicals were moved to shelves where they cannot pose the risk of contamination during the inspection. Ensure that toxic materials are stored separate from food and utensils.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Observed several white powders (flour, corn starch, and tempura batter) in large containers without a label. The PIC labeled the containers during the inspection. Ensure that foods not in their original packaging and easily mistakable are always labeled with the common name.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed single-use utensils at the front service area stored with the food contact surfaces and handles intermixed. The PIC corrected the storage during the inspection. The PIC was educated about the importance of storing handles in the same direction to avoid contaminating the food contact portion. Ensure that single-use utensils are stored in a manner that protects them from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed the floor directly underneath the fryers has an accumulation of grease and food debris. The inspector suggests pulling out the fryers to clean underneath. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Observed personal employee drinks stored on shelves intermingled with and above various food products and clean dishes. The PIC removed all the personal drinks and placed them on a bottom shelf which will be designated as the ‘personal storage shelf’. Ensure that all personal employee items are placed in designated areas.
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed that the PIC’s allergen awareness training is expired. No one else at the facility has completed the training. Ensure that the PIC completes training in basic allergen awareness principles by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed the following food was stored in positions that present a risk of cross contamination: (1) Uncovered containers of food in the walk-in cooler (including, but not limited too, broccoli, rice, and chicken) and uncovered seaweed at the sushi bar; and (2) Raw meat stored over cooked chicken and rice in the walk-in cooler. The various uncovered foods were covered during the inspection. The foods in the walk-in cooler were moved to the correct storage order (ready-to-eat foods above raw foods). Ensure that foods are always protected from cross contamination during storage.  

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces are not cleaned to sight and touch: (1) The baffles of the ice machine; (2) Cutting boards stored on the floor at the sushi bar; and (3) Cutting boards stored behind the faucets of the triple sink. The cutting boards were washed, rinsed, and sanitized during the inspection. The PIC was instructed to store the cutting boards in a new location that does not pose any risk of contamination. There will be a follow-up on 09/20/2024 to ensure the ice baffles have been cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed the left prep cooler was not holding temperatures at 41F or below. The following internal temperatures were recorded: pork 54F, egg yolk 51F, raw chicken 54F, cooked chicken 48F, and dumplings 51F. The food was put into the prep cooler at 10:30 AM. The time the food temperatures were taken during the inspection was 2:30 PM, meaning the four hour period for time-as-control had passed. All food observed at 42F or above was discarded during the inspection (including, but not limited too, pork, egg yolk, raw chicken, cooked chicken, scallops, dumplings, whip cream, and sauce with a mayo base). There were some foods in the middle back portion of the prep cooler that were 41F or below. These foods were immediately moved into a different functioning cooler. The only foods allowed to remain in the cooler were cut vegetables that do not need cold holding. The PIC wanted quick access to chicken that is usually stored in the non-functioning prep cooler. The inspectors discussed using time-as-control during busy operational hours. The PIC was instructed to only remove small amounts of chicken at a time and record the time the chicken was removed from the cooler. The chicken must be discarded after four hours. The chicken should be stored in a different functioning cooler until the facility is busy. 

For information about the cooler, see violation #33.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. The sushi rice is kept at room temperature for four hours, but was observed to not be marked with the time it was brought out during the inspection. Discussed with PIC, who corrected on-site  Ensure the times the rice is brought out for the sushi bar are recorded and discarded after four hours. The inspector will check on time-as-control recording on 09/20/2024.

3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Observed the left prep cooler was not holding temperatures at 41F or below. The PIC stated they will be getting the prep cooler serviced. The inspector will follow-up on 09/20/2024 to check on the left prep cooler temperature. 

See violation #22 for information about the food in the left prep cooler.

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. A gap along the bottom of the back door is present allowing daylight to show through. The PIC serviced the door so no sunlight was observed coming through during the inspection. Ensure that all outer openings are protected against the entry of pests.

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Chips used for soups were observed to be stored in a cardboard box without a liner. Discussed with PIC, who discarded the chips and cardboard box. Ensure ready to eat foods are not stored in bare cardboard boxes.

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed single service utensils at the front pickup area are stored with food contact surfaces and handles intermixed. The PIC was educated and the utensils were moved during the inspection so the handles are facing in the same direction. Ensure that utensils are stored in a position that does not contaminate the food contact surfaces. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces are in need of cleaning: (1) The top of the ice machine where the ice scoop is stored; (2) Containers holding utensils in the service area; and (3) The bar soda gun holder. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to avoid the accumulation of soil. They above mentioned surfaces must be cleaned by the next routine inspection. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
A wire mesh scrubber was in the hand sink during inspection.  Discussed with PIC, who removed it.  Ensure the hand sinks are only used for hand washing.

5-205.11: (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment:
The sushi rice is kept at room temperature for 4 hours, but was observed to not be marked with the time it was brought out during inspection.  Discussed with PIC, who corrected on-site.  Ensure the times the rice is brought out for the sushi bar are recorded and discarded after 4 hours.

3-501.19: (A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
A tub of uncovered breading was being stored on a shelf in the dish room, underneath potentially toxic items.  Discussed with PIC, who corrected on-site.  Ensure toxic, non-food items are stored away from food and food-contact surfaces.

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
A gap along the bottom of the back door is present allowing daylight to show through.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure this gap is sealed to prevent pest/rodent entry.

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Chips used for soups were observed to be stored in a cardboard box without a liner.  Discussed with PIC, who discarded the chips and cardboard box.  Ensure ready to eat foods are not stored in bare cardboard boxes.

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The metal along the top of the hood baffles have an accumulation of grease, which could drip down onto the cooking surface of the stove below.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure this is cleaned regularly to prevent contamination of foods cooking below.

4-601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas needing re-caulking/sealing:
-hand sink by door
-prep sink
-mop sink/basin
-3 part sink
Ensure these areas are caulked to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.
